note: Plan v2 section 8.8 and 9.6. Eight lessons. L3 and L4 are the v2 rewrites; the other six carry over from v1, with L8 reworded only where it named a deleted feature. Terms are marked [[key]] or [[key|display]] and must exist in tooltips.json.

lessons.title: How it spotted your usual stop
lessons.body: The app noticed you buying at the same place, around the same time, three times in two weeks. That is all a [[habit]] means here: a pattern in what you already spend, not a judgement about it. It works from your purchases rather than following you around, and any [[place]] it has noticed can be deleted.
lessons.unlockHint: Unlocks when the app spots your first [[habit]].

lessons.title: Keeping 5% before it's gone
lessons.body: Money that lands in your account tends to leave by Friday. Taking a small slice the moment it arrives means you never feel it go. Five percent of a summer paycheck is a couple of nights out, and it is now yours for years.

lessons.title: The coffee you didn't buy
lessons.body: You skipped one stop, and the money you were about to spend is sitting in your jar instead. Nothing was taken out of your account, because it never left it. That is the whole idea: the cheapest money to keep is the money you have not spent yet.

lessons.title: What a dip is, and what it is not
lessons.body: Prices go up and down every day, and a [[dip]] is a stretch where they are lower than they were. For a fund holding hundreds of companies, past dips have come back, though nobody can promise the next one will, and selling in a panic is the surest way to turn one into a real loss. A single company is different: it can fall and never recover, which is one reason spreading money around matters. You will notice this app never shows you a number going down. It does not watch prices at all, so it cannot panic you with one bad week.

lessons.title: One month in
lessons.body: Thirty days in. Every dollar in the [[jar]] is one you chose to keep, one skip at a time. Look at the total, then imagine that running through every semester and every summer job.

lessons.title: What happens if I need the money for rent
lessons.body: This is your money and you can take it out. Getting money back out of a real investment takes a few days, which is why most people leave the money they need this month somewhere they can reach it, and let the rest sit behind it. Nothing here is locked, it is just out of sight.

lessons.title: Why early money has more time to grow
lessons.body: Money invested now has decades to do its work before you are likely to need it. Money invested later, even if it is more of it, has less time to do the same job. That is not a reason to wait until you have more to put in, it is the reason not to.

lessons.title: You can't really mess this up
lessons.body: There is nothing here to time and nothing to pick. You keep a little, you decide where it goes, and you write down where it went. The main way people lose here is by stopping.
